caption: The drawing depicts the front facade of a building, likely a mission or historical structure, with a large, centrally placed arched doorway at the bottom. The door is wooden, featuring panels and decorative metal studs. Above the door, there is a semi-circular arch made of stone. The building's exterior wall is painted in a pale, off-white or light beige color with areas of exposed red brick indicating aged or worn sections. Directly above the main door, there is a horizontal ledge covered by red clay roof tiles. Above this ledge, there is a central, tall, narrow arched window with a dark interior and a metal grill across the lower section. Flanking the window are four vertical rectangular ornamental elements, two on each side. The uppermost part of the facade also features a short, horizontal ledge with red clay tiles similar to the one below. The bottom of the facade shows brick steps leading up to the doorway. The overall composition is symmetrical, with architectural elements aligned along a central vertical axis. The artist's signature, "K. Meeckinell," appears in the lower right corner.
title: Arched Doorway Mission San Diego
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
